SEOUL, July 27 (Yonhap) -- LG Household & Health Care said Monday that its cosmetics brand The Face Shop will launch five key products, including its Rice Water Bright cleansing line, at about 1,600 Walmart stores across the United States.
The Face Shop's Rice Water Bright line reinterprets the traditional Korean beauty practice of washing the face with rice water and has recorded cumulative sales of more than 49 million units. The line entered Amazon's North American online marketplace in 2024.
Its Rice Water Bright Cleansing Tissues and Rice Water Bright Cleansing Oil have also ranked among the top 10 cleansing products on Amazon.
"The expansion of our offline retail network will help solidify The Face Shop's position as a leading K-beauty brand in the global market," a company official said.

The Face Shop Expands US Distribution Through Walmart Partnership
Posted by Global Cosmetics News | Jul 31, 2026 | Asia & Australasia , North America , Products , Retail |
The Face Shop Expands US Distribution Through Walmart Partnership
THE WHAT?
LG Household & Health Care has expanded the US distribution of its K-beauty brand The Face Shop by launching its flagship Rice Water Bright range in more than 1,600 Walmart stores, significantly increasing the brand’s physical retail presence in North America.
THE DETAILS The rollout includes five products from the Rice Water Bright cleansing range, which has sold more than 49 million units globally and is now available in more than 30 countries.
The Walmart launch builds on The Face Shop’s North American expansion strategy, which began with Amazon in 2024 before extending into Walmart Canada and major US retailers including Target, CVS and Walgreens.
The company said the 20-year heritage of the Rice Water Bright franchise and its continued commercial success have supported its expansion into leading retail chains, with the range recently receiving updated packaging as part of its global growth strategy.
THE WHY?
The agreement demonstrates the continued commercial momentum of K-beauty in the North American mass retail channel. Securing distribution with Walmart strengthens LG Household & Health Care’s international growth strategy while highlighting increasing retailer demand for established Korean skincare brands with proven global sales performance.

Rice Water Revolution: Is The Face Shop Rice Water Bright Cleansing Foam Worth the Hype?
By Himmie Lau Sep 11, 2025
After two decades of watching beauty trends come and go (and trust me, I've seen some real doozies), I've learned to separate the marketing fluff from genuine skincare innovations.
Rice water sits firmly in the "time-tested wisdom" category, and today I'm diving into one of K-beauty's most talked-about products: The Face Shop Rice Water Bright Cleansing Foam.
Pour yourself something refreshing-we're about to get delightfully nerdy about this cult-favorite cleanser!
The Ancient Wisdom of Rice Water
Let's Talk pH (I Promise This Gets Interesting)
Here's something I discovered after testing this cleanser that most beauty influencers conveniently skip over: its pH hovers between 8.0-9.0, which is significantly more alkaline than your skin's natural 4.5-5.5 pH.
During a recent workshop I hosted, a client asked, "But what does that actually mean for my face?" Great question!
Behind That Satisfying Foam Experience
Let's be honest-part of what makes this cleanser so satisfying is that rich, creamy lather. After formulating custom products for clients over the years, I've learned to identify what creates different sensorial experiences.

* Sodium Lauryl Sulfate (SLS) delivering that thorough cleanse
* Myristic Acid creating that creamy stability we all love
* Stearic Acid giving structural integrity to the foam
* Glycerin working quietly behind the scenes to prevent drying

This combination creates a genuinely satisfying cleansing experience, but SLS can be problematic for some skin types. It's like that friend who always gets the party started but sometimes creates a bit of drama in the process.

The Missing Piece: Fermentation
Here's something fascinating I discovered when comparing this product to traditional rice water preparations: The Face Shop's version likely isn't fermented.
Traditional rice water gets much of its magic through fermentation, which:
